title: Finiteness descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ ($X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]) and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$. If $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then $f_i$ is finite for some $i\ge0$ (Stacks Limits, Lemma 01ZO).

source.place: Lemma Tag 01ZO (lemma-descend-finite-finite-presentation, line 1772), in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739); its proof: a finite morphism is affine, so by Lemma 01ZN (lemma-descend-affine-finite-presentation) f_0 may be taken affine; reduce to X_0, Y_0 affine mapping into an affine of S_0, where it is Algebra, Lemma 07RG (lemma-colimit-finite)

proof.text: Because a finite morphism is affine, the hypothesis on f and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] reduce the problem to descending affineness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-stage] to obtain an index after which f_i is affine; replace 0 by that index.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01ZO, proof, first paragraph using Lemma Tag 01ZN

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open covering of Y_0 and refine the inverse images under f_0 by affine opens. Using [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings] and locality of affineness, it is enough to treat one affine pair X_0 -> Y_0 over a common affine open W in S_0; the corresponding base changes at every stage remain affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Lemma Tag 01ZO, proof, reduction after descending affineness to finite affine coverings

proof.text: Write W=Spec(A_0), Y_0=Spec(B_0), and X_0=Spec(C_0) in this affine reduction. The assumption that f_0 is locally of finite type gives that C_0 is a finite-type B_0-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. The limit description [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] identifies the coordinate rings at the limit with A tensor_{A_0} B_0 and A tensor_{A_0} C_0, where A=colim_i A_i.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01ZO, proof, affine reduction in Situation 081D

proof.text: The finite morphism f says that A tensor_{A_0} B_0 -> A tensor_{A_0} C_0 is a finite ring map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-finite-algebra] to obtain i>=0 for which A_i tensor_{A_0} B_0 -> A_i tensor_{A_0} C_0 is finite.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RG (lemma-colimit-finite), applied in Limits, Lemma Tag 01ZO

proof.text: The finite ring map in the preceding step is exactly the affine-local criterion for the base-changed morphism f_i to be finite, by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This proves the assertion for the chosen affine pair and hence, by the finite covering, for f_i.
